business_problem: Intercom needed a flexible AI platform that could keep pace with rapidly changing models while handling large volumes of customer support interactions, complex workflow tasks, and new voice channels at production quality.
solution_summary: Intercom reorganized its product and engineering stack around AI so Fin could move from experimental chat to a durable service platform. The company launched Fin within months of GPT-4, then built a modular architecture that routes support work across chat, email, and voice while swapping in better models as they emerge. Fin handles the conversational support layer, Fin Tasks automates multi-step workflows such as refunds or account changes, and Fin Voice uses the Realtime API for phone-style interactions. GPT-4.1 now powers a growing share of Intercom's AI usage because evals showed it could complete key task flows with strong reliability, lower latency, and a 20% cost reduction versus GPT-4o. Structured offline tests, live A/B experiments, transcript-based benchmarks, and modality-specific voice evals let Intercom move from one model generation to the next in days instead of quarters without rewriting the surrounding system.

data_flow: Customer interactions flow into Fin over chat, email, or voice. The platform routes conversational work to the best model path, invokes Fin Tasks when refunds or other multi-step actions are needed, evaluates behavior with transcript and A/B tests, and feeds connected conversation and ticket data through the MCP Server for downstream product and operations teams.
business_outcome: Intercom launched Fin just four months after GPT-4, replatformed the business around AI, migrated task automation onto GPT-4.1 in days, and reduced cost while increasing reliability and support quality across text and voice channels.
